pr_title: Fix data race when emitting similar Events consecutively
pr_body:

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

There was a data race in the recordToSink function that caused changes
to the events cache to be overriden if events were emitted
simultaneously via Eventf calls.

The race lies in the fact that when recording an Event, there might be
multiple calls updating the cache simultaneously. The lock period is
optimized so that after updating the cache with the new Event, the lock
is unlocked until the Event is recorded on the apiserver side and then
the cache is locked again to be updated with the new value returned by
the apiserver.

The are a few problem with the approach:

1. If two identical Events are emitted successively the changes of the
   second Event will override the first one. In code the following
   happen:
   1. Eventf(ev1)
   2. Eventf(ev2)
   3. Lock cache
   4. Set cache[getKey(ev1)] = &ev1
   5. Unlock cache
   6. Lock cache
   7. Update cache[getKey(ev2)] = &ev1 + Series{Count: 1}
   8. Unlock cache
   9. Start attempting to record the first event &ev1 on the apiserver side.

   This can be mitigated by recording a copy of the Event stored in
   cache instead of reusing the pointer from the cache.

2. When the Event has been recorded on the apiserver the cache is
   updated again with the value of the Event returned by the server.
   This update will override any changes made to the cache entry when
   attempting to record the new Event since the cache was unlocked at
   that time. This might lead to some inconsistencies when dealing with
   EventSeries since the count may be overriden or the client might even
   try to record the first isomorphic Event multiple time.

   This could be mitigated with a lock that has a larger scope, but we
   shouldn't want to reflect Event returned by the apiserver in the
   cache in the first place since mutation could mess with the
   aggregation by either allowing users to manipulate values to update
   a different cache entry or even having two cache entries for the same
   Events.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #92500

issue_context.title: Data race when creating isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".EventRecorder
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

I wrote a test creating multiple isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".[EventRecorder](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/events/interfaces.go#L26) and stumbled upon a data race.

The data race happens in the [recordToSink](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L153) function. It seems that the Event Series field can be read and written at the same time by two different goroutines. [Read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L178) [Write](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171).

This seems to happen in only one scenario:
- (1) a singleton Event is created
- (2) an isomorphic Event is created
- (1) lock addition to cache
- (2) wait for the lock to be released
- (1) unlock
- (2) lock + [create](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171) the Series
- (1) [read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L209) the freshly created Series
- (1) singleton Event is now considered as a series

That being said, this seems to lead to some data inconsistencies as the singleton Event would be created with an unexpected Series.

**What you expected to happen**:

No data race.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

You can run the following code snippet alongside any data race detector. I personally used `go test -race`.
```go
package main

import (
	"testing"

	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
	"k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake"
	"k8s.io/client-go/tools/events"
	"k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/scheme"
)

func Test(t *testing.T) {
	kubeClient := fake.NewSimpleClientset()

	eventSink := &events.EventSinkImpl{Interface: kubeClient.EventsV1()}
	eventBroadcaster := events.NewBroadcaster(eventSink)

	stopCh := make(chan struct{})
	eventBroadcaster.StartRecordingToSink(stopCh)

	recorder := eventBroadcaster.NewRecorder(scheme.Scheme, "test")

	recorder.Eventf(&v1.ObjectReference{}, nil, v1.EventTypeNormal, "reason", "action", "", "")
	recorder.Eventf(&v1.ObjectReference{}, nil, v1.EventTypeNormal, "reason", "action", "", "")
}
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- k8s.io/client-go v0.25.0
